faqs.question: What should legal software include?
faqs.answer: Start with the practice's actual requirements: matter management, client intake, calendaring, documents, billing, permissions, audit history and data export. Requirements differ by practice area and jurisdiction, so validate the exact product and plan rather than relying on a generic checklist.

faqs.question: Is a general CRM enough for a law firm?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. A general CRM may help manage contacts and intake pipelines, but it should not be assumed to replace legal matter management, document workflows, billing or other legal-specific requirements. Compare it with dedicated legal products using the same real workflow.

faqs.question: How should a firm compare legal software prices?
faqs.answer: Request a dated quote for the exact plan and include seats, storage, implementation, migration, training, integrations, support, taxes and renewal terms. Public starting prices alone may not reflect the firm's total cost.

faqs.question: How can we evaluate confidentiality and security?
faqs.answer: Ask for current documentation and contract terms covering access control, audit logs, retention, deletion, backups, data location, incident handling and subprocessors. Verify any compliance claim for the exact product, plan and jurisdiction.

faqs.question: How do we avoid vendor lock-in?
faqs.answer: Before signing, ask for a sample export of matters, contacts, documents, notes and financial records. Confirm export formats, fees, timing, deletion procedures and the help available during migration.

author: Sarah Chen
body:
Legal Software Buying Guide: Practice Management, Intake and CRM

Legal software is not one interchangeable category. A law firm may need matter and case management, client intake, document automation, calendaring, time and billing, legal CRM, or a combination. Start with the workflow and risk requirements rather than a generic “best software” score.

Separate the jobs before comparing vendors

Practice management organizes matters, deadlines, documents and day-to-day legal work. Client intake and CRM manages enquiries, follow-up and client relationships. Document tools help draft, assemble and manage files. Billing and accounting support time capture, invoices and financial controls. A single vendor may cover several jobs, but do not assume that it covers all of them or that every feature is included in every plan.

Build a shortlist around your practice

Dedicated legal products such as Clio, MyCase, PracticePanther, Smokeball, Filevine and Lawmatics can be candidates to investigate depending on the required workflow. A general CRM such as HubSpot may be relevant to contact management, but it should not be treated as a replacement for legal matter management without a documented fit assessment. This guide does not claim hands-on testing, verified ratings, or current prices for these vendors.

Run a repeatable evaluation

  1. Write down five to ten required tasks from enquiry through matter closure.
  2. Mark mandatory needs separately from preferences, including jurisdiction, practice area, confidentiality and accounting requirements.
  3. Ask each vendor to demonstrate the same sample workflow using realistic data.
  4. Record pass, partial pass, fail and unknown for each requirement; link every claim to current vendor documentation or contract language.
  5. Test exports and permissions before uploading sensitive production information.
  6. Obtain a written quote and calculate total cost over the intended contract period.

Questions to ask before signing

  • Which exact product and plan includes each required feature?
  • How are permissions, audit history, retention, deletion and backups handled?
  • Which integrations are native, paid add-ons or dependent on third parties?
  • Can the firm export matters, contacts, documents and financial records in usable formats?
  • What are implementation, training, support, renewal and termination costs?

Pricing and evidence limitations

Vendor prices and plan details change. This page does not publish unverified numeric prices or ratings as facts. Ask vendors for a dated quote that specifies the plan, users, region, implementation, storage, add-ons and renewal terms. Verify security and compliance claims against current documentation for the exact product and contract.

Bottom line

Choose the product that passes the firm's mandatory workflow, confidentiality, export and cost checks—not the product with the highest unsupported score. Keep the evaluation notes and quote together so the decision can be reviewed when requirements or contract terms change.
